identifier_scope.evidence_note: Health Canada MDALL has no primary/package DI concept: its identifier table publishes one device_identifier string per device row. ATLAS assigns scheme='di', scope='global', is_primary=1 to any 14-digit value. The US primary/package distinction is GUDID's own identifiers[].type.

resolved_vs_pairs_arithmetic.note: ATLAS reports bridge_fda_records_resolved=942 and pairs=934. The 8 extra records are records returned by a query for a separator-form MDALL identifier ('0 8800022 30080 3'): the response's primary DI is the bare 14-digit form, which is NOT a key in ATLAS's mdall_views dict (that dict is keyed by the raw string), so the pair is dropped.

firm_attribution.note: Health Canada's MDALL identifier table publishes no company name. ATLAS fetched 40 MDALL licences; the company links it derived are name-alias resolutions (13 exact_alias tier, 8 candidate tier) and all resolve to GE HealthCare. HORIZON's independent 60-licence slice does not overlap the 66 licences behind these 934 pairs. So at most 9/934 pairs (1.0%) have any Canada-side company attribution, and 925/934 (99.0%) have none in the local frozen data. Corporate coherence on both sides is therefore NOT established for this bridge.
